newsitem.title: UK: New UK gilts settlement system starts Aug 97-BOE.
newsitem.headline: New UK gilts settlement system starts Aug 97-BOE.

text.p: The Bank of England said the new electronic settlement system for gilts, using the same software as the Crest computerised share registration system, would be introduced on August 26, 1997.
Previous plans were for it to start in the spring of 1997.

"But an extension in the timetable is sensible to enable market firms to concentrate in the immediate period ahead on the current transition of equities settlement from Talisman to Crest," the Bank said in a statement.
The introduction of strippable gilts will also be delayed by a few months.
The Bank said the Central Gilts Office and Crest had agreed to use the same networks (Syntegra and Swift) to keep open the option of consolidating the two systems in future.
"This represents a significant and concrete step forward in convergent development of the two systems," the Bank said.
Strippable gilt facilities would be delayed and would now start "a month or so" after the upgraded settlement service is introduced.
"Regardless of the date for the start of the strips market, gilts which are to be strippable will pay gross from June 7, 1997," the Bank said.
